questions.question:
Study the questions based on the information given below.

A certain number of people standing in a line facing north.There are only 4 people standing between K and L. L stands to the right of P, who stand third to the right of M. THere are only 3 people standing between K and M. J is the only neighbor of L. O stands fourth to the right of Q. Minimum 2 people standing between J and O. M standing at the extreme left end of the line.3 person standing between P and N, who stands near to R. S is one of the people.

Who stands third to the left of O?
questions.explanation:
The given puzzle is solved by the following steps.

4 people standing between K and L. And 3 people standing between K and M, Who stand at the extreme left of the line.

L stands to the right of P, who stands third to the right of M. J is the only neighbor of L

3 people stand between P and N, who stand near R.

O stands fourth to the right of Q. And at least 2 people stands between J and O.S is one of the people

So it is clear that S stands third to the left of O.

questions.question:
In the question below there are three statements followed by two conclusion I and II. You have to take the three given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the three statements disregarding commonly known facts.

 

Statements:

All Music are Songs

Only Songs are Lyrics

At least some Songs are Singers

Conclusion:

I. Some Singers can be Music

II. No Lyrics is Singer
options: Both Conclusion I and Conclusion II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II follows
questions.explanation:
Conclusion:

I. Some Singers can be Music: Follows (As there is no direct relation between the elements so possibility is true)

II. No Lyrics is Singer: Follows (As Only Songs are lyrics so no lyrics is singer is true)

From the figure, both conclusion I and conclusion II follows. Hence, option A.

questions.question: A,B,and C enter into a partnership. A advances Rs.1600 for 4 months ,B advances Rs.1600 for 8 months and C advances Rs 1000 for 10 months. They gain Rs.730 altogether. Find the profit share of B.
questions.explanation:
The profit should be divided among A ,B and C in the ratio of their capital \(\times\) time

i.e in the ratio 1600\(\times 4\ \): 1600\(\times 8\ \): 1000\(\times 10\)

= 6400 : 12800: 10000

=16: 32 : 25

Given total profit = Rs.730

Adding all ratios we get 16+32+25 = 73

Share of x = \(\frac{\text{ratio of x}}{\text{total of ratio}}\)\(\times \text{total profit}\)

B’s share = \(\frac{32}{73}\) of 730 = Rs.320

questions.question: The average of present age of Anjali ,Babita and Chandani is 31 years. If age of Anjali is two years less than that of Babita and age of Babita is eight years less than Chandani, then Find the present age of Anjali.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Average age of Anjali, Babita and Chandani = 31 years
• Anjali is 2 years younger than Babita
• Babita is 8 years younger than Chandani

Calculation:
Let Babita = x

Anjali = x − 2
Chandani = x + 8

Average = 31

(x − 2 + x + x + 8) / 3 = 31

(3x + 6) / 3 = 31

3x + 6 = 93

3x = 87

x = 29

Anjali = 29 − 2 = 27

Alternate Method:
Average = 31
Total = 31 × 3 = 93

Let Babita = x
Then Anjali = x − 2
Chandani = x + 8

Sum = x + (x − 2) + (x + 8) = 3x + 6

3x + 6 = 93

3x = 87

x = 29

Anjali = 27

Hence, option (D) is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Average formula
• Linear equation
• Assumption method

questions.question: In a Library 60% of the books are in Urdu, 60% of the remaining books are in Hindi.Rest of the books are in English, if there are 9600 books in English, then the total number of books in Urdu is ?
questions.explanation:
Let the number of books in library = x,

Then, Number of Urdu books =  0.6x,

Remaining books = x - 0.6x = 0.4x

=> 60% of remaining books is Hindi =  0.6×0.4x = 0.24x

=> Number of English books = x - 0.6x - 0.24x = 0.16x

Given, 0.16x = 9600.

So, x = 60000

Hence, No. of Urdu books = 0.6  ×60000=36000

questions.question: Two candidates fought an election. One of them got 62% of the total votes and won by 864 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.explanation:
Ans. 3600

Winner got 62% votes

So, the loser will get (100 – 62) = 38% votes.

Let total votes be 100x.

So,

62% of 100x – 38% of 100x = 864

62x – 38x = 864

24x = 864

\(x\  = \frac{864}{24} = \ 36\)

Required answer = 3600

questions.question: A man purchased a table. He spent ₹180 on its maintenance and ₹60 on its transportation. If he sold it at ₹1800 and earned a profit of 25%, then find the purchased price of the table?
questions.explanation:
Let the purchased price of the table = ₹‘x’

So, total amount spent on the table = (x + 180 + 60) = ₹(x + 240)

Now,

\(1800\  \times \ \frac{100}{125}\  = \ x\  + \ 240\)

x = 1200

Purchased price of the table = ₹1200

questions.question: A platform of length 250m is crossed by a train of length 150 m. If the speed of the train is 72 kmph, then find the total time taken by the train to cross the platform.
questions.explanation:
Total length of platform and train \(= \ 250 + 150\  = \ 400\ m\)

Speed of train = 72 kmph\(\  = \ 72 \times \frac{5}{18}\  = 20\ m/s\)

Time taken to cross the platform \(= \ \frac{400}{20} = \ 20\ sec\ \)
